notes.meaning: Saul was fiercely determined to destroy the followers of Jesus. Threats and murder had become like the very air he breathed. He went to the high priest in Jerusalem to get official backing for his violent crusade.

Saul asked for letters to the synagogues in Damascus so he could arrest any believers he found, both men and women, and bring them back in chains. Early believers called their movement 'the Way,' meaning a whole life devoted to following Jesus. Saul did not even spare women, which showed how cruel and relentless his anger was.

As Saul came near Damascus, a brilliant light from heaven suddenly flashed all around him. Other accounts tell us this happened at midday, and the light shone brighter than the noon sun. This was the glory of the risen Jesus appearing directly to him on the open road.

The blinding light knocked Saul to the ground, and he heard a voice calling his name twice. Jesus asked why Saul was persecuting Him. Because Jesus and His church are united as one, hurting His people is the very same as hurting Christ Himself.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explained that Christ speaks as the head of the church, showing that the Head shares the pain of His body.

notes.meaning: Saul asked who was speaking, and the voice replied, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.' Saul was shocked to learn that the crucified teacher from Nazareth was alive and speaking from heavenly glory. Resisting God only brings pain and defeat to the person who fights Him.

differ.view: Saul was born again right here on the road when he surrendered to Jesus as Lord.
Saul was brought under deep conviction on the road, but his conversion was not completed until faith came in Damascus.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars note that the proverb about kicking against the goads was not in the earliest Greek manuscripts of this verse, but was added by later copyists from Acts 26:14.

notes.meaning: Jesus commanded Saul to stand up and go into the city of Damascus, where he would receive further instructions. Christ chose not to reveal the full plan at once, but gave him only the next step to test his obedience. God often teaches proud people humility by sending ordinary believers to instruct them.

The men traveling with Saul were left speechless with shock. They heard the sound of the voice, but they could not understand the words or see anyone. Their experience served as independent proof that a real, supernatural event had just taken place.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching explains that the companions heard an audible sound like thunder, but only Saul was given to understand the distinct words spoken.

notes.meaning: Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes, he was completely blind from the brilliance of Christ's glory. His companions had to take him by the hand and lead him into Damascus. The proud persecutor who intended to lead believers away in chains was now as helpless as a child.

For three days, Saul remained totally blind and did not eat or drink anything. He spent this time deeply troubled by his past sins and praying to God. This intense darkness helped strip away his self-righteous pride and prepared his heart for new life in Christ.

The Lord spoke to a disciple in Damascus named Ananias in a vision, and Ananias readily answered. Ananias was not an apostle, but a respected and faithful local believer. God often uses ordinary Christians to accomplish His greatest purposes.

The Lord gave Ananias exact directions to go to Straight Street and look for Saul of Tarsus at the house of Judas. God noted that Saul was praying. The persecutor who once recited formal prayers as a Pharisee was now truly crying out to God for mercy.

The Lord explained that Saul had already seen a vision of a man named Ananias coming to place hands on him so he could see again. God prepared both men beforehand to bring them together in peace. This assured Saul that Ananias was a true messenger sent from God.

Ananias hesitated and told the Lord about the terrible harm Saul had done to the saints in Jerusalem. Saints is a word for Christians, meaning those set apart as holy to God. Ananias was honest about his fears, even while talking with the Lord.

Ananias pointed out that Saul had arrived with official power from the chief priests to arrest all who called on Jesus' name. Calling on the name of Jesus was how early Christians prayed and publicly showed their faith in Him. Ananias wondered why he should go meet a man who had come to arrest him.

The Lord told Ananias to go anyway, revealing that Saul was His chosen instrument to spread His name far and wide. Saul was appointed to carry the gospel to Gentiles, to earthly kings, and to the people of Israel. God can turn His fiercest enemy into His most useful servant.

The Lord declared that He would show Saul how much he had to suffer for His name. The man who had caused so much suffering for others would now endure hardship and pain for the sake of Christ. Suffering for Jesus is not a sign of God's anger, but a normal part of serving Him.

Ananias obeyed God, went into the house, and laid his hands on Saul with the warm greeting, 'Brother Saul.' He announced that Jesus, who appeared to Saul on the road, had sent him so that Saul could regain his sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit. Ananias welcomed the former persecutor as a true member of God's family.

differ.view: Saul was converted on the road but filled with the Holy Spirit three days later, showing that being filled with the Spirit is an experience separate from salvation.
Being filled with the Spirit here refers to being empowered for ministry, rather than receiving a distinct second blessing after conversion.

notes.meaning: Immediately, something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and his physical sight was restored. He stood up right away and was baptized as an outward sign of following Jesus. The sudden cure showed God's miraculous power and confirmed that Ananias had spoken the truth.

differ.view: Saul had to rise up to be baptized, which points to full immersion in water rather than being sprinkled while sitting.
Saul was already forgiven by faith, so baptism served as an outward seal and confirmation of the grace he had already received.
Baptism is the means through which Jesus puts our old self to death and gives us new life, washing away the blindness of unbelief.

notes.meaning: Saul ate food after his three days of fasting, and his physical strength returned. He then spent several days in Damascus with the local disciples. The man who had traveled to arrest these Christians was now gladly enjoying their fellowship.

Without delay, Saul began preaching in the Jewish synagogues of Damascus, declaring that Jesus is the Son of God. He used the very meeting places where he had planned to hunt down believers to proclaim the truth about Christ. Real conversion gives a person a deep desire to tell others about the Savior.

Everyone who heard Saul was completely astonished by his sudden change. They remembered that he had violently persecuted believers in Jerusalem and had come to Damascus specifically to arrest them. A radically changed life is powerful proof of the reality of the gospel.

Saul grew stronger and bolder in spirit, confounding the Jewish leaders in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ. Christ is the title for the Messiah, God's promised Savior and King. Saul skillfully connected biblical prophecies to Jesus' life to show that He is the promised Redeemer. God's truth has the power to silence opposition.
